Yes—look for **“Sauerteigbrot”** on the menu. These Munich bakeries explicitly offer sourdough bread:

- **Julius Brantner Brothandwerk** — Three locations: Schwabing (Nordendstraße 23), Altstadt (Kreuzstraße 1) and Haidhausen (Pariser Straße 38). Its rotating range includes organic breads; the sourdough baguette is listed for Saturdays. ([julius-brantner.de](https://www.julius-brantner.de/en/))
- **Bageri** — A small bakery in the Schlachthofviertel at Adlzreiterstraße 21. Its breads are leavened exclusively with sourdough. It’s open Thursday–Sunday, and bread is sold while supplies last. ([bageri.de](https://bageri.de/menu))
- **Hofpfisterei** — A Munich bakery chain with many branches and a large range of natural-sourdough breads, including rye and whole-grain loaves. ([hofpfisterei.de](https://www.hofpfisterei.de/hpf_sortiment_natursauerteigbrote.php?utm_source=openai))
- **REIS** — In the city’s south, with its main bakery in Solln at Festingstraße 4 and other local branches. It describes its rye, mixed-rye and spelt loaves as sourdough breads. ([plasma.cafe](https://plasma.cafe/brot/))
- **Bäckerei Zöttl** — Has multiple Munich locations; its Bauernlaib is made with the bakery’s own sourdough. ([zoettl.de](https://zoettl.de/))

For a dedicated sourdough bakery, **Bageri** is a good bet; for a wider choice of traditional rye-style loaves, try **Hofpfisterei**. Check opening hours and daily availability before heading out.
